extracted.intended_audience: researchers (particularly Wellcome-funded) and authors considering where to publish; advocates of open science
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors about publishing research outputs on the Wellcome Open Research platform, focusing on openness in article types, data sharing, and open peer review practices. Emphasises compliance with Wellcome funding open access requirements and platform-specific policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy and price transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: All the policies are clearly described on the website, including details on price transparency, explaining what the article processing charge that Wellcome pays per article is used for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the platform policies for clear information about fees (the article processing charge Wellcome pays) and other publishing policies; price transparency is presented as a core platform standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepts a diverse array of article types
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome Open Research accepts a diverse array of article types, providing the option to publish every aspect of a research project, from conception to the final Research Article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Research Articles, Method Articles, Data Notes, Study Protocols and other non-traditional types; authors are encouraged to publish outputs beyond a single Research Article to capture fuller project details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage publishing non-Research-Article outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing other outputs other than Research Articles allows for a much deeper analysis and review of each stage of the project and, subsequently, a much richer academic discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method Articles are highlighted as particularly relevant because the methods section of a Research Article is often shortened; authors should consider separate Method Articles or other outputs when material does not fit the Research Article narrative or word limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that any associated data be made openly accessible alongside the articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open data means freely and openly sharing information or materials collected, created, or reused as part of a research project (survey results, gene sequences, code, neuro-images, audio files, etc.). Sharing supports reproducibility, corroboration, and richer peer review feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Data principles compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome Open Research’s open data policy supports the FAIR Data principles as a framework to promote the broadest reuse of research data and secure its longevity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare data to be findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR) to maximise reuse and longevity; platform policy frames FAIR as the operative standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘As open as possible, as closed as necessary’ data rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The open data policy aims to ensure that research data is made ‘as open as possible, as closed as necessary’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All data and supporting materials must be shared unless there are commercial, privacy, security, or confidentiality concerns; authors must justify restricted access where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review practices taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review can include a range of practices: Open identities; Open reports; Open participation; Open interaction; Open final version commenting; Open platforms ('decoupled review').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists these varieties to illustrate that open review is not one single model; authors and reviewers should be aware which practices apply in a given context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wellcome’s open peer review model (post-publication and fully open)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review at Wellcome Open Research is post publication, with articles published before peer review is undertaken; and fully open, with reviewer identities, affiliations, and reports being published alongside articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect articles to be visible immediately and reviews (with reviewer names/affiliations) to be published openly; this model aims to speed dissemination and increase accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applied across all outputs and soundness-focused review
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review is applied across all outputs, including non-traditional article types, and focuses on the soundness of science over author reputation or perceived novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review criteria emphasise methodological soundness and validity rather than novelty or the authors’ reputations; this applies to Research Articles, Method Articles, Data Notes, Study Protocols, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative and developmental review (co-reviewing option)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review is collaborative, with the option for early career researchers to work with senior researchers by co-reviewing articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform encourages mentorship and collaborative reviewing practices that provide developmental opportunities for early career researchers; authors and reviewers can expect that co-reviewing is supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of post-publication open review (speed, accountability, credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-publication peer review speeds up publishing times and subsequently accelerates research impact. Transparency adds accountability and gives credit to the reviewers by publicising their names and reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors gain faster dissemination and potentially earlier feedback; reviewers receive public credit which may validate expertise to authors and the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and compliance with Wellcome funding open access requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome Open Research publishes results originating from Wellcome-funded research and offers an option for publishing in full compliance with the open access requirements set out in their grant agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors of Wellcome-funded research should use this service to meet funder open access mandates; check eligibility and compliance details on the platform.
